scope: Fixed-seed two-base demand-location contrast. Swap the station assignments of the accepted F03.var02 depot-only risk unit and the one-aircraft second unit, with their mission preparation and turnround rows. Depot routes, stock, resources, repair, PM, schedules, seed and 60-hour window stay fixed.

parameters.stock: zero BASE-01 and BASE-02 LRU opening stock; two depot LRU positions
parameters.route: symmetric two-hour BASE-01/BASE-02 to DEPOT-01 legs

expected_timeline: The accepted parent exhibits three risk-fleet LRU demands at BASE-01. The control arm should reproduce those source identities and events if a descriptive-only change is inert.

The station-swap arm should place the two-aircraft risk unit and its fault-driven LRU demands at BASE-02 and the one-aircraft BASE2 mission at BASE-01. Do not assume random draws or event timing are invariant until checked against native output.

Compare station-scoped item demand, physical transport origin/destination, base backorder and repair/mission events. Aggregate reports may be identical for symmetric capacities and routes; do not infer per-base demand from aggregate bins alone.
acceptance_hypotheses: Two fresh serial guarded SSH0/mutex/GUI13340 native runs import/export/calculate/report, have zero conversion errors and no unreviewed diagnostics, roundtrip all populated authored tables and seal raw evidence.

The pair changes only unit station and associated mission preparation/turnround station fields as a coherent demand-location switch, plus descriptive text. Stock, resource, repair/PM and depot-route business rows are identical.

A bounded demand-location claim requires traceable aircraft and item IDs, matched or explained fault/demand sequence, correct station-scoped transport and inventory ledger, aggregate System/Stock/Resource half-hour bins, and terminal disposition. Other demand timing, route asymmetry, interbase transfer and larger-network effects remain outside scope.
